#2122. How Dave Challinor honed his craft with Celtic, Brentford trips before taking Sheffield Wednesday job

Out-of-work managers often take the time out of the spotlight to evolve their coaching game, and this was no different for new Sheffield Wednesday boss Dave Challinor. Between leaving Stockport County and taking the SWFC job, the 51-year-old has revealed Celtic’s Martin O’Neill and Brentford boss Keith Andrews’ influences.

In an interview with The Star, Challinor revealed he had dinner with O’Neill, alongside watching his Celtic side train and play. On O’Neill, the Owls boss said: “He is a really inspirational character. He is a figurehead for that football club. The success he’s had at such a massive place is enormous.”

Challinor then toured Brentford’s training ground and took inspiration from how the Bees prepare for set pieces.

“Brentford, I suppose for any club in England, or across the world, really, just the way they go about it and the way they’ve done it from the very, very top, is unbelievable,” he said. “They are an inspiration not just to me as a manager, but I’d suggest football clubs the length and breadth of the country.”

Challinor has plenty of experience in the dugout, but for someone who has followed his trajectory, there is always more to learn. He has journeyed through the football pyramid from Colwyn Bay to Sheffield Wednesday in 16 years, so he can take valuable lessons from those who have pedigree at a higher level.

In terms of his managerial abilities as an individual, Challinor will have taken plenty from O’Neill at Celtic. The 74-year-old progressed through lower leagues like the Sheffield Wednesday boss before managing big clubs in top leagues, such as Leicester City, Celtic and Aston Villa.

The sheer amount of knowledge and experience O’Neill has gained over the years means he will have had some valuable nuggets of advice to pass down to Challinor.

As for Brentford, touring their training ground would have been more of a lesson in full club management, and what can help traditionally ‘smaller’ clubs compete with the elite. The Bees are not the wealthiest club by any means, but they are sustainably run from the top to the bottom, and meticulous training sessions and match preparation means they are now in their sixth season as a Premier League side.

Challinor will have taken valuable lessons from these trips, and it will only benefit SWFC.

David Storch has expressed that Sheffield Wednesday are just at the start of a long-term rebuild. Challinor was not appointed with immediate success in mind, he was brought in to lead a new era at Hillsborough.

Some of the Hillsborough faithful will expect a strong push for promotion from League One this season, and justifiably so. Despite Storch stating the need for patience, the squad is strong enough to emerge as a strong contender at the top end of an evenly matched third tier.

Challinor’s willingness to learn and take inspiration from other managers and model clubs is an excellent attribute. Despite the success he has found in the dugout already, his desire to grow as a boss is only a good thing for SWFC as they rebuild under his leadership.

#2121. L'Inter ripensa a Mosquera e ritrova la ThuLa. Chivu avrà i suoi bomber contro l'Atalanta

L'Inter a poco più di un mese dall'inizio del mercato di gennaio torna a pensare all'acquisto di un difensore... per l'estate. Nel mirino dei nerazzurri c'è una vecchia conoscenza della dirigenza di Viale della Liberazione, ovvero Cristhian Mosquera. Il centrale piaceva già qualche anno fa, ora però veste la maglia dell'Arsenal, ha un contratto fino al 2030 e vale non meno di 30 milioni di euro. Ancora è presto, ma Baccin un tentativo con i Gunners lo farà.

Un libro non va mai giudicato dalla copertina e questo è un suggerimento che ci sentiamo di dare anche a tutti i tifosi dell'Inter, che sui social e in rete erano preoccupati alla vigilia della sosta per le nazionali dopo gli infortuni di Bonny e Thuram, con Lautaro Martinez e Luis Henrique che erano ancora ai box. #2120. Zabatta: “Verso gli Stati Generali dello Sport, una grande festa per tutta la Campania”

Zabatta: “Verso gli Stati Generali dello Sport, una grande festa per tutta la Campania”

Presentata in Consiglio regionale l’iniziativa del 22 novembre alla Mostra d’Oltremare. Una giornata ad ingresso libero tra campioni, scuole, associazioni e cittadini.

Una giornata per riunire il movimento sportivo campano, valorizzarne i protagonisti e promuovere una pratica sportiva sempre più accessibile e inclusiva. È “Verso gli Stati Generali dello Sport 2026”, l’iniziativa promossa dall’Assessorato allo Sport della Regione Campania, presentata questa mattina nella Sala Caduti di Nassiriya del Consiglio regionale.

L’appuntamento è per domenica 22 novembre alla Mostra d’Oltremare, Padiglione 3B , con incontri, premiazioni, attività dimostrative e occasioni di confronto tra istituzioni, federazioni, associazioni, scuole, atleti e cittadini.

Alla conferenza stampa hanno partecipato l’assessora regionale allo Sport Fiorella Zabatta, il presidente del Consiglio regionale Massimiliano Manfredi, Sandro Cuomo, campione olimpico nella spada a squadre ad Atlanta 1996, e l’atleta paralimpica Angela Procida.

“Vogliamo che sia una grande festa dello sport campano, un’occasione per dare spazio a ogni disciplina, a ogni talento e a ogni storia. Lo sport è passione, sacrificio e inclusione, una palestra di vita che unisce generazioni e crea comunità. Con questa iniziativa, unica nel suo genere in Campania, vogliamo riunire chi vive lo sport ogni giorno: dagli atleti alle associazioni, dalle scuole alle federazioni, fino alle famiglie. Il nostro obiettivo è costruire uno sport davvero accessibile, perché non deve essere un privilegio legato alle possibilità economiche, ma un diritto e un’opportunità per tutti”, ha detto l’ assessora regionale allo Sport Fiorella Zabatta.

”Gli Stati generali dello sport devono segnare l’avvio di una nuova stagione di impegno e di politiche concrete per la Campania. Lo sport non è un lusso né un privilegio, ma un diritto e un fondamentale strumento di crescita, salute, educazione e inclusione sociale. La nostra sfida è garantire a ogni cittadino, indipendentemente dal territorio in cui vive o dalle proprie condizioni economiche e personali, la possibilità di praticarlo. Servono investimenti negli impianti, sostegno alle associazioni e alle società sportive e una particolare attenzione ai giovani, alle persone con disabilità e alle fasce più fragili. Il Consiglio regionale è pronto a fare la propria parte: dobbiamo trasformare le tante energie del mondo sportivo in una visione comune e in azioni concrete. Perché investire nello sport significa investire nel futuro, nella coesione e nella qualità della vita della nostra comunità. La Campania ha bisogno di una politica dello sport che non lasci indietro nessuno”, ha aggiunto il presidente del Consiglio regionale Massimiliano Manfredi.

Il programma del 22 novembre inizia alle 9.30 von l’accoglienza dei partecipanti; alle 10.30 apriranno gli stand delle Federazioni sportive campane. Alle 11 il convegno “Sport e scuola: educazione, inclusione e benessere” darà il via alla sessione mattutina, che proseguirà con le premiazioni di “Napoli Capitale Europea dello Sport” e i riconoscimenti alle scuole, alle associazioni e alle realtà che si sono distinte nella promozione della pratica sportiva.

Alle 18 si terrà il convegno “Presente e Futuro dello Sport in Campania”, seguito dalle premiazioni della Presidenza del Consiglio regionale e dai riconoscimenti ai grandi protagonisti dello sport, tra cui la campionessa olimpica di ginnastica artistica Manila Esposito, altri atleti e rappresentanti delle Federazioni sportive.

Per tutta la giornata sarà possibile visitare gli stand, conoscere e provare diverse discipline sportive e partecipare alle attività dimostrative. Alle 20 è previsto lo show cooking “La dieta dello sportivo”.

L’iniziativa è organizzata dall’Assessorato allo Sport della Regione Campania, con la partecipazione del CONI Campania, del Comitato Italiano Paralimpico (CIP), di Sport e Salute e di Padelness e Sport, con il supporto operativo di Sviluppo Campania. L’ingresso è libero .

#2119. 3 managers Swansea City must target ASAP as Vitor Matos leaves for France

Swansea City have been dealt a big blow ahead of club football’s return this weekend. RC Strasbourg are set to appoint Vitor Matos as their new boss after reaching a compensation agreement with the South Welsh side.

It marks a significant blow for the Swans, given Matos’ success and short time in the job. The Portuguese coach has been in charge at the Swansea.com Stadium for just shy of a year, and has turned them into Championship play-off contenders with impressive and intense pressing football.

Now though, a replacement must be identified. Here, we put forward three contenders that Swansea City should consider…

If Swansea City want Championship pedigree and a similar coaching profile to Matos, then Carlos Corberan is the ideal candidate. The Spaniard is available after being let go by Valencia earlier this season, and although reports have said he’s eyeing a top-flight job, the chance to lead a Championship promotion push will be tempting.

Corberan likes his sides to press intensely and high up the pitch, much like Matos. He took inspiration from Marcelo Bielsa, who he worked under at Leeds United, and has found a great level of success.

No compensation fee would be required, yet Corberan would still be an exciting and ambitious appointment.

Next up is Belgian boss Karel Geraerts, who is also out of work and thus wouldn’t require a compensation fee. Many at Swansea City will wonder whether Jamestown Analytics influence the search for Matos’ replacement, and if they do, Geraerts could come into consideration.

The 44-year-old was manager of Union SG for the 2022/23 season and oversaw 35 wins in 57 games. They scored 116 goals in the process and averaged 2.04 points per game before FC Schalke came calling.

That stint didn’t work out for Geraerts, and he was sacked in his last job by Stade Reims after missing out on Ligue 2 promotion. However, his similar high-pressing tactics and focus on wide overloads would fit the Swans’ squad.

At 34 months, Geraerts falls just short of the 36 months of head coach experience needed to be granted automatic qualification. However, through the Exceptions Panel, his Jupiler Pro League title challenge and run to the UEFA Europa League quarter-finals with Union SG would likely see this approved.

Last but not least is Mike Tullberg, who also falls short of the required head coach experience. But, like Geraerts, Swansea City would likely be successful in an exception appeal given his UEFA Pro License, elite pedigree at Borussia Dortmund and immediate silverware wins at FC Midtjylland.

The 40-year-old took charge of the Danish club in 2025, finishing 2nd and winning the Danish Cup in his first season. He held a variety of roles at Borussia Dortmund from 2019 to 2025, including a brief spell as their caretaker boss which yielded two wins and a draw.

Tullberg’s side are currently unbeaten in the Danish Superliga with nine wins and five draws. He too focuses on high-pressing football, allowing for continuity after Matos’ exit. As he is in a job and under contract until 2029 though, the Swans will have to pay compensation for his services.

#2118. Calciomercato no stop - Indiscrezioni, trattative e retroscena del 17 novembre

L'Inter guarda in Premier League per rifondare il proprio pacchetto arretrato e mette nel mirino il difensore dell'Arsenal, Cristhian Mosquera. Nato nel 2004 ad Alicante, il 22enne difensore è uno dei giovani difensore più interessanti in Europa. Arrivato a Londra nell’estate del 2025 dal Valencia per poco più di 20 milioni di euro, oggi vanta una valutazione superiore ai 30 milioni e un contratto in scadenza nel 2030. Il centrale dopo aver giocato in tutte le selezioni giovanili della Spagna, è entrato nel giro della Nazionale maggiore.

Anche l'Inter pensa a Oliver Provstgaard, grande rivelazione con la maglia della Lazio. Il nativo di Copenaghen avrebbe conquistato gli osservatori nerazzurri, secondo La Repubblica: la squadra meneghina sarebbe interessata a lui per sistemare la propria retroguardia, su richiesta esplicita di Cristian Chivu, che in lui vedrebbe la soluzione ideale per un ruolo ad oggi senza un reale proprietario. Lotito però rappresenta un ostacolo non da poco Il presidente della Lazio non svende i propri gioielli, a maggior ragione oggi che stanno sfoderando prestazioni sorprendenti. E secondo la testata la richiesta per privarsi del nazionale danese a gennaio sarebbe di ben 40 milioni di euro. Per questo, sempre in ottica difesa, in Viale della Liberazione si continua a monitorare la situazione di Mario Hermoso, il cui contratto con la Roma scadrà nel giugno 2027. Ad oggi non c'è un accordo tra le parti ma la volontà sembra quella di trovarlo. Ad ogni modo, in caso di mancata intesa, il club nerazzurro potrebbe avanzare un'offerta.

Il mercato di gennaio potrebbe riportare Manu Kone al centro delle trattative. Il centrocampista della Roma è finito nuovamente nel mirino della Premier League: Manchester United e Chelsea stanno valutando un possibile affondo, con l'intenzione di convincere i giallorossi attraverso un'offerta importante.

Gerry Cardinale è pronto a investire ancora sul Milan. A gennaio come detto la priorità resta sicuramente il difensore centrale. Gonçalo Inacio dello Sporting Lisbona è senza dubbio il preferito anche se servirà un investimento da almeno 40 milioni di euro, ammesso che il club portoghese abbia voglia di privarsene a metà stagione. Tra le alternative restano Sylla dell’Union Saint-Gilloise, Ganiou del Lens e Reggiani del Borussia Dortmund. Sicuramente tra un paio di settimane la strategia sarà definita nei particolari. E per il dopo Modric, la pista da seguire porta a Stiller dello Stoccarda.

Come spiegato dal giornalista Matteo Moretto sul canale YouTube di Fabrizio Romano, i rossoneri stanno seguendo con grande attenzione l'evoluzione di Enzo Perez, promettente centrocampista classe 2008 in forza all'Oviedo, nella Serie B spagnola. Moretto ha riferito che gli emissari del Milan sono andati a vederlo dal vivo a più riprese nelle ultime settimane e nei mesi scorsi. Il giocatore, che ha una clausola di rescissione e sta trovando continuità d'impiego, è finito nel mirino anche di altri club tra cui Chelsea, Espanyol, Betis e Brentford. L'Oviedo vorrebbe trattenere il ragazzo, ma la sua permanenza dipenderà dalle offerte in arrivo: la società spagnola è infatti consapevole di poter concludere l'operazione di mercato più importante della propria storia.

Come vi abbiamo raccontato, la Fiorentina va alla ricerca di un nuovo terzino sinistro nel calciomercato di gennaio e una mano al DS viola Fabio Paratici nella sua caccia all'uomo giusto potrebbe arrivare da un procuratore molto influente e amico del dirigente, il portoghese Jorge Mendes. Quest'ultimo infatti deve trovare una nuova sistemazione a un suo assistito di Serie A, e la Fiorentina potrebbe essere la soluzione giusta. Secondo una rivelazione del portale FirenzeViola.it, infatti, Mendes avrebbe proposto al club gigliato il profilo del nazionale ecuadoriano Pervis Estupinan, a tutti gli effetti un giocatore in esubero nel Milan.

Nelle score ore è emersa un'indiscrezione da Napoli che, se confermata, avrebbe un peso specifico non indifferente nell'economia delle situazioni in essere nella società partenopea in maglia azzurra. Sarebbe infatti pronta la proposta da parte del presidente De Laurentiis per estendere il contratto dell'attuale direttore sportivo Giovanni Manna fino al 30 giugno del 2032.

Il rendimento di Gustavo Varela non è passato inosservato e il mercato si prepara a muoversi attorno all'attuale capocannoniere della Serie A. Il centravanti portoghese del Monza è diventato un obiettivo concreto di Juventus e Napoli, entrambe intenzionate a giocare d'anticipo già nella sessione invernale per evitare un'asta internazionale in estate. I partenopei seguono il classe 2005 da diverse settimane, ma nelle ultime giornate anche la Juventus ha intensificato i contatti, sia con la dirigenza brianzola sia con l'entourage del giocatore, rappresentato dall'agenzia Leaderbrock. Il Monza valuta il suo attaccante 35 milioni di euro: una cifra importante, che le due pretendenti vorrebbero ridurre inserendo una contropartita tecnica. Il Napoli potrebbe proporre Giovane, Folorunsho o Ngonge, mentre i bianconeri valutano di mettere sul tavolo uno dei propri giovani. La concorrenza, però, non arriva soltanto dall'Italia. Il Tottenham ha già preso informazioni direttamente con i rappresentanti del giocatore, mentre il Brighton ha mandato più volte i propri osservatori a visionarlo dal vivo. Anche il Manchester United ha seguito Varela durante Monza-Atalanta, quando un emissario dei Red Devils era presente al Brianteo. Sullo sfondo c'è inoltre il Barcellona, che ha effettuato un primo sondaggio in vista della prossima stagione.

Il futuro di Kevin De Bruyne potrebbe essere nuovamente in Premier League. Il centrocampista belga, arrivato al Napoli nell'estate del 2025 dopo dieci anni al Manchester City, starebbe valutando la possibilità di lasciare l'Italia già durante la prossima sessione invernale di calciomercato. Le difficoltà incontrate in azzurro, tra problemi fisici e risultati al di sotto delle aspettative, avrebbero alimentato una crescente insoddisfazione. Nonostante un contratto in scadenza nel giugno 2027, l'ipotesi di una separazione anticipata comincia a prendere consistenza. Trovano conferme le voci provenienti dall'Inghilterra. Gli agenti del belga avrebbero già avviato contatti esplorativi con Brentford, Crystal Palace e Fulham per verificare la disponibilità dei tre club londinesi ad accoglierlo a gennaio. Sullo sfondo rimarrebbe anche l'interesse dell'Everton.

Dominic Vavassori è uno dei migliori giovani messi in luce in Serie B in questa stagione. Sei gol e un assist a trascinare il Palermo al primo posto della classifica, tanto da accostarlo ai club di medio alta classifica in Serie A. In particolare è il Napoli ad avere già chiesto informazioni all'Atalanta che, da par suo, non ha grande intenzione di cederlo. Attualmente è in prestito secco ai rosanero e le prestazioni suggeriscono la possibilità di tenerlo per la prossima annata.

L''Atalanta ha comunicato il rinnovo di Lorenzo Bernasconi. Terzino sinistro, prodotto del vivaio dell'Atalanta, andrà a guadagnare 500 mila euro a stagione, più 200 di bonus. Sembra però più un rinnovo ponte che un assestarsi su cifre definitive. Giustamente l'ottimo rendimento della scorsa stagione - quello discreto di questa - ha portato i nerazzurri a ritoccare verso l'alto, ma è chiaro che rimane uno dei meno pagati della rosa nerazzurra, anche per il valore che ne ha dato la scorsa estate: 25 milioni di euro.

L'Atalanta guarda ancora una volta ai giovani talenti emergenti e, secondo le informazioni riportate da Fanatik, ha inserito nella propria lista anche Furkan Dursun, attaccante classe 2005 del Thun. Il centravanti austriaco, già nel giro della Nazionale Under 21, sta vivendo una stagione da protagonista in Svizzera: in 19 presenze ha realizzato 9 gol e fornito 5 assist, numeri che hanno convinto la società bergamasca a seguirne con attenzione la crescita.

In casa Venezia si lavora in vista della prossima sfida contro la Juventus, ma la dirigenza pensa a porre le basi per il futuro. Decisivo contro l'Udinese è stato un gran gol di Kike Perez, che con Davide Nicola in panchina ha mostrato un ulteriore step di crescita. Il suo contratto è a scadenza nel 2027, ma ci sono stati già dei contatti per parlare di prolungare il rapporto: Kike Perez è importante per il Venezia, un posto dove si è legato a doppio filo. BARCELLONA, BALDE PUÒ PARTIRE GIÀ A GENNAIO: MANCHESTER UNITED ALLA FINESTRA. GVARDIOL IL SOGNO DI FLICK, PIACE ANCHE BASTONI. REAL MADRID, JJ GABRIEL SALUTA I RED DEVILS. ARSENAL, ACCORDI PER I RINNOVI DI RICE, TIMBER E RAYA. DERBY COL CHELSEA PER KROUPI. LIVERPOOL SUL TALENTO BRASILIANO ARTHUR DIAS. TOTTENHAM, OCCHI SU OH HYEON-GYU: IL BESIKTAS CHIEDE 30 MILIONI

Giornata di incontri importanti in casa Barcellona, dove Jorge Mendes ha fatto visita a Lamine Yamal e Alejandro Balde. Se con il primo il procuratore portoghese ha discusso principalmente delle condizioni fisiche, con il secondo si è parlato soprattutto di mercato. Il terzino non è soddisfatto dello spazio concessogli da Hansi Flick e valuta la possibilità di lasciare il club già a gennaio. Tra le possibili destinazioni figura il Manchester United, che aveva chiesto informazioni sul giocatore già la scorsa estate, al pari di Manchester City e Bayern Monaco. Lo stesso Balde sarebbe attratto dalla prospettiva di giocare in Premier League. In entrata, invece, il Barcellona continua ad apprezzare Josko Gvardiol, ma l'operazione appare quasi impossibile sia per le difficoltà economiche dei catalani sia per la volontà del Manchester City di trattenere il croato, sotto contratto fino al 2031. Tra le alternative resta Alessandro Bastoni.

Il Real Madrid si prepara ad accogliere uno dei talenti più promettenti del calcio inglese. JJ Gabriel ha salutato ufficialmente il Manchester United attraverso un video pubblicato sui propri canali social. Il gioiello classe 2010, che ha riscritto diversi record nelle giovanili dei Red Devils, firmerà un contratto triennale con i Blancos e sarà inizialmente aggregato alla formazione Juvenil A, prima di poter vestire la maglia del Castilla a partire da gennaio.

Giornate particolarmente intense anche in casa Arsenal, con Andrea Berta al lavoro per blindare i protagonisti del progetto tecnico di Mikel Arteta. Declan Rice ha raggiunto un accordo per prolungare il proprio contratto fino al 2031, con un aumento dell'ingaggio che dovrebbe portarlo a guadagnare circa 300mila sterline a settimana, al pari di Bukayo Saka. Intesa raggiunta anche per il rinnovo di Jurriën Timber, mentre David Raya ha trovato un accordo verbale con la società londinese fino al giugno 2030. Anche per il portiere spagnolo è previsto un adeguamento dello stipendio, con la firma attesa a breve. Tra i prossimi giocatori a prolungare il proprio legame con i Gunners potrebbe esserci anche Piero Hincapié.

Possibile derby di mercato tra Chelsea e Arsenal per Eli Junior Kroupi, attaccante francese classe 2006 del Bournemouth, reduce da una stagione da 13 gol in Premier League. Entrambe le società londinesi stanno monitorando il giocatore in vista della sessione invernale. Il Chelsea, in particolare, è alla ricerca di nuove soluzioni offensive e apprezza la duttilità del francese, utilizzabile sia da centravanti sia da esterno sinistro. Nel mirino dei Blues è finito anche un altro giocatore del Bournemouth, il centrocampista Alex Scott.

Il Liverpool guarda invece al mercato sudamericano per rinforzare la difesa. I Reds si sono inseriti nella corsa ad Arthur Dias, centrale classe 2007 dell'Athletico Paranaense, già protagonista di oltre 50 presenze tra i professionisti. Il giocatore piace anche a Tottenham, Barcellona, Bayer Leverkusen e Lipsia. Gli Spurs avevano presentato un'offerta da circa 20 milioni di euro la scorsa estate, rispedita al mittente dalla società brasiliana, che ora valuta il cartellino 30 milioni. Il contratto del giovane difensore scadrà nel dicembre 2028.

Lo stesso Tottenham sta valutando un investimento per il reparto offensivo e ha messo gli occhi su Oh Hyeon-gyu, attaccante sudcoreano del Besiktas. Arrivato dal Genk per 14 milioni di euro, il classe 2001 viene utilizzato da Vincenzo Italiano principalmente come alternativa a Dusan Vlahovic. Il club turco non vorrebbe privarsi del giocatore, legato da un contratto fino al 2029, ma potrebbe prendere in considerazione una cessione davanti a un'offerta da almeno 30 milioni di euro.

#2117. Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair

Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic new look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP

Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

Haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a new campaign.

It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

“I’ll try to find a new Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager said. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup. Then he joined the club and then after he achieved many important things. Now the target for us is to try to find the new Rodri.

“When David Silva was here, everyone was worried - Kevin [De Bruyne] arrived. When Sergio Agüero was here, everyone was worried – Erling [Haaland] arrived. When Ferdinando left, Rodri arrived. It’s just about this.

“When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”

Maresca added: “Hopefully we can do the things that we need to do. It doesn’t help that there are players that for different reasons want to leave, this is for sure.

“But we need to adapt and we don’t want to keep players here that don’t want to stay.

“The normal thing in transfer windows is that you have to wait because all the clubs try to keep players until the last week and then sell for more money.

“It’s normal, I’m not worried about that. When the transfer window closes and we have all the squad there, for sure it will be different.”

#2116. Enzo Maresca tinkers his way to nervy Man City win

Few in elite sport have the luxury of managing their own endings as Pep Guardiola did at Manchester City, yet no one can ever fully control a beginning. Enzo Maresca’s City started their Premier League season with a win, in the end, but three points masked the scale of the job he faces.

The narrative focus has been the impossibility of filling the personality void Guardiola leaves at a club sculpted in his image. That macro reading overlooks the number of distinct issues with City that Maresca must fix. A new midfield has to be recruited then blooded, a jittery defence needs settling down, and Phil Foden clearly requires help to recover the form which made him Premier League player of the year as recently as 2024.

All of that can wait after this victory against Bournemouth, which quietened some of the alarms from last weekend’s 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in Cardiff. Josko Gvardiol scored an injury-time winner after City had trailed for most of the match, much of it a sloppy slog for the home side, who went behind in the 26th minute. The introduction of Rayan Cherki for Nico O’Reilly revived some familiar attacking effusiveness.

A lesser-spotted VAR-aided double celebration capped a tense but ultimately joyful day for Maresca. Marc Guéhi equalised from Cherki’s well-taken corner in the final minutes, then the expanded Etihad Stadium rapturously celebrated Gvardiol’s apparent winner, only to see it flagged offside. Video assistant Paul Howard intervened to show Gvardiol was onside from Cherki’s pass, before City’s fans, players and staff shouted twice as loud for twice as long to salute a morale-boosting victory.

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

“It’s the perfect day to be honest,” Maresca said, although he may wish to set his expectations slightly higher. The East Stand which faces the dugouts at the Etihad unfurled a banner before the game welcoming him back to Manchester after his spell as Guardiola’s assistant. “I was very pleased when the game started, to watch the banner at the other side, and I was pleased at the end because we gave them the joy of the three points.”

His team made a fluid and furious start to Premier League football, suffused with a desire to prove the Community Shield is just a jumped-up friendly. A newly streamlined short-haired Erling Haaland ran with impatience, Elliot Anderson was a sinewy presence in midfield, Foden pulled off a gorgeous flick which led to a shot by Rico Lewis, well saved by Djordje Petrovic.

Maresca’s selection was surprising, with six defenders in his XI, some deployed unexpectedly. Guéhi partnered Anderson in defensive midfield, while their England team-mate O’Reilly was often just behind Haaland in a No 10 role. There was an air of destiny about one O’Reilly run down the left flank in the first half, cruising to the byline and crossing presentably. Haaland was well positioned in the middle, but utterly fluffed his lines. Samson similes on standby, although perhaps he too was short of full match fitness during his early-season visit from the Philistines?

Momentum shifted after Haaland’s miss, and Bournemouth took the lead when an innocuous high ball flummoxed Abdukodir Khusanov and Rúben Dias. They both pursued it, neither could make decisive contact and it left Evanilson on the ball with space to manufacture an unmissable cross for Marcus Tavernier.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

Marco Rose, their new manager, is facing a similarly daunting task to Maresca in living up to a predecessor who led Bournemouth to their highest-ever league finish and European football. “How the game went, it was quite unlucky to lose,” he said. “We had two situations, one corner kick and one attacking when we defended too passive, and that’s why we lost.”

His team showed an appealing coiled-spring quality after weathering the early City onslaught. They have players of class with the ever lively Tavernier, new signing António Silva seamlessly replacing Marcos Senesi at centre-back and silky Alex Scott, the Guernsey Grealish, whose current standing has now overtaken the man who gave him his nickname.

They could not hang on here though, with Guéhi atoning for a free header planted wide with his day-saving equaliser. Cherki’s corner was nodded in from around the six-yard line then, with the game in the balance, the Frenchman provided another, thanks in part to the semi-automated gods smiling on Gvardiol and his new manager.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

City will need more, especially in midfield. Anderson at his best can cover the ground and roles of two men, which is just as well as City await reinforcements. The incoming Ayyoub Bouaddi will help, but it is a big ask for an 18-year-old to fill a spot vacated by a Ballon d’Or winner. Maresca was asked after the match about finding a “new Rodri” and deadpanned “Marc Guéhi”, who played acceptably, but is probably not a long-term solution.

There was a jadedness at times from City, which is not a great way to start the season, although they will surely improve with a bolstered squad and fitness levels. Maresca said “four or five” of his players who returned late from the World Cup are still effectively in pre-season training, including Haaland and Anderson.

Of course City are not the finished article, what team are one game into a new season? While there is a vast gap from this performance to their best, it was still impressive to smuggle three points from zero with six minutes left to play. Guardiola’s influence will be hard to shake, but that need not be a negative.

Marc Guéhi: Central Midfield Edition pic.twitter.com/ViBZqOroB2

The Maresca era begins with the most dramatic of wins. City were trailing 1-0 at 84 minutes, but somehow managed to turn it around.

Emery doesn’t hang around. I’m not convinced he shook Hurzeler’s hand.

Manchester City 2 Bournemouth 1 (Gvardiol) Oh my, Gvardiol has the ball in the back of the net but his “winner” is ruled out by the linesman instantly. Cherki had wriggled this way and that on the edge of the box before sliding in the Croatian who dispatched the ball with aplomb.

BUT, replays show that Hill’s back foot played Gvardiol onside ...so the late, late goal is GIVEN!

Maresca jumps for joy, the Etihad erupts. But that is heartbreaking for Bournemouth...

Joško Gvardiol scores in stoppage time! 👊 pic.twitter.com/FrTrfIg3ur

Guehi saves the day for City, scoring a harder header than the sitter he missed early in this half. Nice corner from Cherki was powererd in from close to the penalty spot. Crowd smells blood with five minutes left but Bournemouth look to still have a bit in the tank.

Incidentally, Jack Grealish is on for City with the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ Alex Scott still out there for Bournemouth, who is presumably worth about double in today’s transfer market? Can’t be often that a player shares pitch with his nickname-giver as their careers head in opposite direction. Wonder if Lionel Messi was ever described as “the new Roman Riquelme?” and played against him?

Bournemouth have responded well to getting pegged back, playing through City, who are desperate for a shot at three points. Gannon-Doak stands up a cross but finds the gloves of Donnarumma.

City attempt to break down the left but Grealish just runs out of road.

Manchester City 1 Bournemouth 1 (Guehi) He might have missed a sitter earlier on, but when presented with a similar opportunity from a corner - this time via Cherki from the right - Guehi makes no mistake, planting his header beyond Petrovic.

No mistakes this time from Marc Guehi 😤 pic.twitter.com/xlCJXWUzz6

Haaland threatens to break free down Bournemouth’s right but Truffert just about recovers and clears his lines.

Grealish replaces Foden, who slopes straight down the tunnel.

Jebbison calls Donnarumma - who has been a spectator for the past 20 minutes - into action with a sharp header. There is a delay in the taking of the subsequent corner as Adams and Jebbison jostle for position with the City goalkeeper, but it’s all for nothing as the delivery is dealt with.

Foden goes into the book for a foul on substitute Jebbison. A tad harsh, perhaps. Looks like he semi-slipped into that contact.

Ayari attempts an bicycle kick but cannot beat Bizot. That would have been a goal of the month contender had it found the back of the net.

Guehi combines with Foden down the right and hits the by-line before a digging out a cross to Haaland. The ball is behind him and his right-footed effort does not have the requisite power to beat Petrovic, who has been immense today.

Bit better from City, Foden curls just wide, Semenyo has a shot well saved by Petrovic. Meres presence of Cherki seems to have injected some urgency to their attacks and fear to Bournemouth’s defence. Not sure City look quite ready for this season. Obviously there will be further incomings but they are leggier and more haphazard than Bournemouth.

Chance! Foden, Nunes and Cherki work the ball from right to left on the edge of Bournemouth’s box, eventually falling to Haaland who scoops the ball over with his usually lethal left boot. The visitors had plenty of men between ball and goal and that caused the Norwegian to snatch at his effort.

Villa started last season with no win in their first five games and just three points. They then rallied strongly after that. This one feels different as the rebuild is so significant. Second half has been very flat so far.

City are asking questions now. Cherki combines with Foden down the right and the Englishman shifts the ball on to his favoured left boot and his curled effort deflects off Silva and out for a corner which comes to nothing.

Semenyo breaks free down the left channel and fires the ball across the keeper towards the far post, but Petrovic gets a strong hand to it and pulls off a good save.

Kostoulas thinks he’s made it five having followed in a fizzed-in Costinha effort that had struck the post. But the strike is scrubbed off immediately and replays back up the linesman’s decision.

Little sign of City finding the composure to take control of this match. Passing is getting ever-sloppier and Guehi put a free header painfully wide. Maresca’s team are dominating possession but would be no surprise if the next goal was another Bournemouth sucker-punch. Kovacic and Cherki about to come on, the latter should improve the picture.

Anderson receives treatment on the pitch and is subsequently replaced by Kovacic. The Englishman stretches out his right leg as he leaves the field of play and keeps it elevated as he takes his position on the bench.

Dunk creates some chaos in Villa’s box, spinning in a lofted through-ball which Bizot palms away under duress. Rutter then pulls an effort wide off the resulting corner.

Nunes makes an instant impact, beating Scott easily down the right before standing up a cross to the far post where Haaland is waiting. Two Bournemouth defenders mirror the forward’s leap and do enough to disrupt his flow - and Semenyo’s - the Ghanaian also misses the ball.

Shows how few options Emery has - he has not made a change at half-time. Villa have been a little brighter going forward. A good run from Hemmings to play in Maatsen, and then the Villa teenager misjudging a cross when McGinn put him in down the right. But Brighton will feel there are more goals for them.

Maresca looks to his bench and brings on Nunes for Lewis.

Brighton are still going for this. Gross’ corner from the left reaches Vuskovic at the back post, but he cannot poke the ball past Bizot.

You’ll do well to see a worse miss all season! Guehi is afforded the freedom of Manchester inside the box from an inswinging corner but he somehow glances the ball wide.

"That is an EXTRAORDINARY miss!" 🫣Marc Guehi misses a golden opportunity to equalise for Manchester City! pic.twitter.com/Jl96MMmQeP

De Cuyper tees up another corner from the right. His punched-in delivery picks out Ayari perfectly on the edge of the box but the Swede’s volley flies just wide. A touch ball to hit first time.

Villa have opted to sit in and hope they can see this out without further damage. The Sky Sports cameras pan to a now sparse away end where some are still cheering their side on. Fair play.

Play has resumed at the Etihad and immediately City begin circulating the ball in front of Bournemouth’s first line of pressure. It’s all very slow still and they are unable to penetrate their opponents’ robust mid-black.

Boos at half time as City leave the field, although will charitably assume they are more for referee Jared Gillet for his late non-award of a penalty. Rico Lewis went down in the box but it looked soft. Another early test for Maresca, Bournemouth are lively in attack and defending capably. City all pace and intent but not playing with much patience or finesse.

Pretty horrifying first half from Villa. It was a strange team to start with – factoring in the four big summer sales and then the two absentees, Watkins and Emi Martinez. But this has been even worse than expected. Many of the team has just crumbled under the first sign of pressure. Pau Torres has been terrible. Joao Gomes picked up a yellow and then a red card on his debut. Villa started with Buendia as a centre-forward and now - with ten men - are just trying to play without any striker at all. Emery’s options are limited. Funny to think they started really well and should have taken the lead through Buendia on five minutes.

There’s a shout for a penalty as Haaland knocks down a header at the back post for Lewis, who gets shoved to the ground clumsily by Scott. Nothing going though, and that’s the half.

There’s a coming together on the halfway line at the Etihad. Haaland and Silva tangle, which sets off a chain reaction as Kluivert comes steaming in, first towards Haaland and then Guehi. Evanilson is next on the scene and he gets a firm shove off Gvardiol.

City now looking shaky at the back. Cross-field balls in their half zipping past half a dozen in sky blue without intervention, shots from range going just wide, Donnarumma needing to save well to prevent a second.

Has stopped clicking up front as well, something isn’t going to plan when you have Haaland in your team but most of the high balls are heading towards Foden and O’Reilly.

CARTÃO VERMELHO! Gomes is sent off. Disaster for Villa. It was a kick at Rutter borne of frustration. McGinn was already walking Gomes away from referee Peter Bankes before the decision came. A clear kick to the chest after Rutter knocked him over. Gomes has been nowhere near the level required. He will never forget his Villa debut.

Ooof, Tavernier goes close with a lovely curled effort from 25 yards out. Just wide, however.

Kluivert gets a sight at goal moments later but is denied by Donnarumma who gets down to his left sharply to keep the ball out.

Haaland looks to breathe life into City’s rather drab performance by chasing down Petrovic.

Moments later, he directs a glancing header towards goal and forces the Bournemouth keeper into a smart stop. Foden’s subsequent corner is not up to much.

VAR is looking at an incident on the halfway line. Rutter barges into Gomes and the midfielder kicks out at the Brighton front man. The referee is sent to the screen and a red card correctly follows. A dreadful performance from Gomes.

Villa have really struggled under pressure at the back. Going forward they still look have enough creative players that they are not embarrassed. But Brighton are dominating them with the press in the Villa half. There are not many options for Emery to change at half-time. Mings? Garnacho?

Some very untidy defending for the opening goal here which comes against the run of play, if not drastically so. Khusanov was bamboozled by an  innocuous high ball, couldn’t make decisive contact and left space for it to reach Evanlison on the right, whose cross was hard for Tavernier to miss.

A few groans and grumbles already from the home fans, Guehi getting some flak for squandering a decent position near the Bournemouth area and giving away the ball. Not really his job to be on the ball and making stuff happen near the opposition box though, is it?

This is looking very bad for Villa. Two Brighton goals in one minute for Jack Hinshelwood and it is 4-0 with 31 mins played. The first was a very well-worked goal – Ayari cross nodded down by Gomez for Hinshelwood to head in. The second was just another mistake by Villa – Ayari stealing the ball from Joao Gomes to create a critical turnover. Villa started well but they look completely outgunned physically. Brighton are really pressing home their advantage in the duels. Lots of pressure on the likes of young George Hemmings and Gomes.

"Absolutely INCREDIBLE!"Jack Hinshelwood scores two in a matter of minutes and Brighton are ripping Aston Villa apart! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tvS5qMJJ8C

Brighton 4 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) That’s two in a matter of seconds. Again, Villa try to play out from the back and again they get caught out. Ayari telescopes in a leg to take the ball away from Gomes on the edge of Villa’s box and Hinshelwood is there to tuck it home.

Brighton 3 Aston Villa 0 (Hinshelwood) A cross from the left is nodded back across goal by Gomez and Hinshelwood is there to finish.

Manchester City 0 Bournemouth 1 (Tavernier) Bournemouth carve City open with ease. A long ball from Smith is not dealt with and Rayan works the ball out to Evanilson who needs just a brief look up before picking out Tavernier, who finishes at the back post.

Marcus Tavernier fires Bournemouth ahead against Manchester City! 💥 pic.twitter.com/lSyNRfrTlc

City have not yet reached the intensity levels they usually show when in full swing. Semenyo tries to inject some energy with a burst down the left but Rayan does well to track back and cut it out.

Villa’s defence is floundering. This time a corner delivered from the right sails over everyone, including Bizot, but the back-post nod-down evades everyone and Villa clear their lines.

Bright start from City, but momentum has diminished since an odd miss from Haaland, whose limbs looked unusually muddled after O’Reilly soared down the left wing and crossed presentably. Move had an air of inevitability to it, was unexpected not to see the Norwegian score. Prepare the Samson similes.

The second goal from Brighton, and it’s direct. Georginio Rutter played through with a very straight ball, and Rutter had Pau Torres on the proverbial toast. De Cuyper kept up with his team-mate and ran onto the cross. Villa have not been bad. Torres, however, is having a dreadful afternoon.

Brighton 2 Aston Villa 0 (De Cuyper) Rutter does brilliantly to latch on to a ball over the top from well inside his half. He bursts down the left channel before lashing a fierce ball across the face of goal which De Cuyper turns in. Villa in all sorts of problems here.

What a start for Brighton!Maxim De Cuyper doubles their advantage! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/3WbyZlEhMV

Chance! O’Reilly bursts past Smith out on the left and picks out Haaland, who appears to be in two minds as to whether he wants to head or volley the ball. Instead he does neither and the chance goes begging.

Gomes leaves one on Ayari, which is risky given he has already picked up a booking. A red card at this point would be hugely damaging.

Brighton take the lead with an own goal from Victor Lindelof. An unfortunate one for the Swede who was trying to get Maxim De Cuyper’s shot off the line. It hit the post and ricocheted in off Lindelof. The fault lay with Pau Torres who gave the ball away needlessly. Very good turn from De Cuyper to make the room for the shot. Up until then, Villa - even with this unusual understrength side - were much the better.

Lewis is in fact playing right-back, with Guehi into defensive midfield alongside Anderson. O’Reilly advanced of both, with Gvardiol at left-back. All quite fluid, though, as you would expect from modern City.

Brighton 1 Aston Villa 0 (OG Lindelof) A disaster at the back for Villa. Pau Torres looks to play out from near the by-line but instead picks out De Cuyper inside Villa’s box. The wide man does well to steady himself before getting a shot away, which ricochets off the post, back on to Lindelof and into the net.

City have started brightly. Here Haaland slips in Lewis, who is unmissable with his new bleached hair, but Petrovic pulls off a smart save.

Chance! Ayari gets his pocket picked inside his own half by a buzzing Barkley. Buendia has a sight of goal but he slides the ball inches wide.

He’s at it again moments later, but he sends a third effort at goal over the bar.

Villa have started the brighter of the two sides. McGinn spins a deep free-kick into the box, which is cleared out to Buendia on the edge of the box but his shot sails over.

A warm minute’s applause for the former Manchester City manager.

Brighton are in their customary blue and white home kits shooting left to right, with Villa in black.

That’s a “Welcome Back Enzo” banner slowly cascading down the East stand. Feel that the tifo department has missed a trick, because it would have been very amusing to use a picture of Pep Guardiola, and see if anyone noticed. That could actually be Guardiola for all I know, my facial recognition is dreadful. Getting all of the trite “don’t they look similar!” observations out of my system ahead of the September cut-off point.

The teams have emerged from the tunnel at the Amex and the Etihad...

When asked by Sky Sports whether Ollie Watkins’ omission from the match-day squad was a sign that his Villa career was over, Emery pursed his lips and stared back at the reporter for a few seconds before saying: “Silence.”

After being pressed on the subject, he added: “No, no, no. We are playing today here. It’s OK. We are not speaking about [Ollie].”

"Silence" 🤫An unusual response from Unai Emery 😅 pic.twitter.com/kWNZtQu3PA

On taking charge of his first match as City head coach, Enzo Maresca told Sky Sports: “It’s big emotion. It’s a very nice feeling, the first game at home in front of our fans, so hopefully we can give them the three points.”

When asked about Elliot Anderson and the void left by Rodri, he added: “I think Elliot [Anderson] has to be himself; a good player, he’s going to be even better, but he has to be himself. Again, for me, there are no players that they are the same player, they are all different.

“We are happy with Elliot, but for sure, as we know, Rodri is a big player but he’s already gone. So now the focus is on the ones that are here with us and the ones that will probably arrive.”

Brighton have spent around £100m this summer but of those only the Croatian centre-back, Luka Vušković, is in the starting XI to face Aston Villa. He cost £46m from Spurs. Brighton have, as ever, sold players with Jan-Paul Van Hecke the biggest price. The expectation is that Carlos Baleba will leave for Manchester United. He is not in the squad. The injured Yankuba Minteh would not have been involved today - but he is another likely departure. Player of the year Ferdi Kadioglu is missing with injury.

Pep Guardiola’s successor assessed the breadth of the challenge before him and offered a candid appraisal of how to replace the irreplaceable. “It would be silly to try and change it,” he said of Guardiola’s grand design.

Tito Vilanova was addressing the world’s media in Camp Nou. For Barcelona in 2012, read Manchester in 2026. Enzo Maresca would be wise to study the manual for standing on the shoulder of a giant.

Charged with maintaining the standards of a two-time Champions League-winning team many still consider the best ever, Vilanova’s big idea was effectively to leave the existing one alone, mastering the art of the subtle tweak.

Describing the transition as seamless barely does justice to the changeover; Vilanova’s Barcelona side won 23 of their first 25 La Liga matches, snatching back the title lost to Real Madrid in Guardiola’s farewell campaign. Tragically, the promise of further honours to build on sturdy foundations was realised by others as Vilanova died from cancer in 2014.

After a brief stint by Gerardo Martino, Luis Enrique gave the dream team of Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta and Sergio Busquets further La Liga titles and another Champions League win.

The so-called “impossible job” of being bound by the weight of the preceding genius, therefore, was no such thing.

The Villa team is missing six of the players who started the Europa League final against Freiburg on May 20. Four of them have left (Ezri Konsa, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne, Youri Tielemans) and Emi Martinez and Ollie Watkins might be leaving too - they are absent today. Belgian goalkeeper Marco Bizot starts and there is also a place for teenager George Hemmings. Emi Buendia in what looks like the central striker role. It is certainly a bracing opening day to the season for Unai Emery.

No sign of Watkins in what is an objectively underpowered Aston Villa line-up. There’s also no start for new signing Suzuki, with Emery preferring Bizot between the sticks. Academy graduate Hemmings makes his first Premier League start.

Some eyebrows raised at the inclusion of Rico Lewis in City’s starting XI, presumably as a defensive midfielder given the presence of Dias, Guehi, O’Reilly and Khusanov on the team-sheet. He did not have a pleasant afternoon in Cardiff last weekend, although that could be said for several City players. Some lingering doubts about his physicality, in a Premier League becoming ever more hands-on, but Enzo Maresca knows him from his time as an assistant here and clearly rates him. Wonder whether that sentiment will endure if (when) City buy some new midfielders in the coming weeks.

Haaland will make his 200th appearance for City this afternoon. Either Lewis or O’Reilly could be deployed alongside Anderson in central midfield.

Welcome to live coverage of Sunday afternoon’s 2pm Premier League kick-offs. Enzo Maresca faces the unenviable task of following Pep Guardiola’s decade of dominance at Manchester City and his reign begins in earnest with a visit from Bournemouth, who themselves are ushering in a new era after Marco Rose succeeded Andoni Iraola. A bruising 3-0 defeat in the Community Shield last weekend does not bode well for City’s hopes of closing the gap to Arsenal, but Maresca will be telling his charges that this afternoon is a fresh start: a new week and a new competition, plus Erling Haaland has a new haircut…

The Italian’s squad has been shorn of World Cup winner Rodri, who departed for Barcelona this week, and the spotlight will turn to £116m club-record signing Elliot Anderson who is expected to make his Premier League debut with City. Jérémy Doku is out for two to three weeks after suffering a calf injury, which could open the door for Jack Grealish, with City bereft of wide options. City will have their work cut out as Bournemouth, fresh off a historic sixth-place finish last season, look to extend their 18-match unbeaten run from the end of last season. The Cherries won three of their five pre-season matches, which included an eye-catching 10-1 victory over Serie A side Genoa.

Brighton and Hove Albion welcome Aston Villa to the Amex for their 2026-27 season opener having travelled 220 miles north of the Arctic Circle to play Norwegian side Tromso in their Europa Conference league play-off on Thursday. Fabian Hurzeler’s side face the defending Europa League champions without Carlos Baleba, who is on the brink of joining Manchester United, as well as injured wingers Kaoru Mitoma and Yankuba Minteh. While Unai Emery has lost key players in Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa and Lucas Digne, the funds raised has gone towards seven signings, with Zion Suzuki, the Japan goalkeeper, in line to make his first start for Villa.

#2115. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”

#2114. Don Goodman delivers brutal Bolton Wanderers warning

Bolton Wanderers have had a rollercoaster first third of the campaign upon their return to the Championship, and though the Trotters have impressed at the top end of the pitch, a lot has been left to desire at the back.

Bolton, following their return to the Championship for the first time since 2019, endured an incredibly busy summer transfer window orchestrated by head coach Steven Schumacher, with as many as 13 new arrivals heading to the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

Among those was an almost entirely new forward line, as the likes of Jayden Nelson, Ryan Hardie, Thelonius Bair, Kylianne Dong, and Samuel Iling-Junior joined the club.

Bolton have hit 20 goals in 15 league matches so far - a steady record. However, with 29 shipped in the other direction, improvements must be made at the back, as an EFL expert has shared their thoughts on the situation.

Football League World has asked AI to predict the 2027/28 EFL Championship table if Manchester United and Manchester City were in it

Former West Bromwich Albion, Sunderland, and Wolverhampton Wanderers striker Don Goodman has delved into punditry since his retirement from professional football, and has garnered a reputation as an expert on everything in the EFL.

The 60-year-old is not afraid to say exactly what he thinks about the ongoing situations at clubs across the 72, and has shared his thoughts and concerns right now at Bolton, saying: "If you go to watch Bolton Wanderers, you know you're in for a terrific match.

They have been all season. They're a great watch.

"I suspect Steven Schumacher wants them to be entertaining, but here's the issue. They are conceding way too many goals. That will prove costly over a 46-game season.

"They've conceded 29 goals in 15 games. That's almost two goals a game. It means you have to score three goals to win a match. That might happen occasionally, like when they won 4–3 away at Norwich, but it's rare you can rely on scoring three every week.

"They have to become harder to score against. If they don't, I fear they could end up straight back in League One. They're great fun to watch, but they must tighten up defensively."

Only the bottom three of Preston North End, Burnley, and Derby County have shipped more goals than Bolton at this stage of the season, as it has become crystal clear exactly where Steven Schumacher's side needs to address if they are to be successful this year.

Despite this, only Stoke City, Sheffield United, Birmingham City and Swansea City have kept more clean sheets than the Trotters' four after 15 games, as when Bolton concede, it tends to come in waves.

They have conceded three or more goals in seven games this season, as Schumacher simply must find a way to keep the scoreline to a minimum if his side is to pick up enough points for survival come the end of the campaign.

A seven-point buffer separates them from the relegation zone right now, but it could take just a couple of weeks for that to change, as Bolton cannot afford to continue to ship goals at the rate they have been.

What have you made of Bolton Wanderers this season? Is Don Goodman's assessment of the Trotters correct? Share your thoughts below!

Schumacher has worked his way up the league to establish himself as one of the best young coaches in the EFL, having earned promotion to the Championship with Plymouth Argyle and Bolton, whilst keeping Stoke afloat in the second tier against the odds.

Now, he must try and establish the Trotters back in the second tier after seven years away, and whilst on track to do just that as things stand, if the defensive record doesn't improve sooner rather than later, he runs the risk of slipping down the table.

Goodman's warning must be taken into account by Schumacher, who should use the recent international break as an opportunity to do just that.

#2113. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2112. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

#2111. EFL star facing jail risk for major on-pitch incident and it's caused a stir

A York City star could be facing the threat of potential jail time for a shock incident that actually occurred on the pitch - and it's causing quite the reaction as a controversial legal battle begins to gather pace.

York finally ended their ten-year exile from the EFL in emphatic fashion at the end of the previous campaign by finishing at the summit of the National League table on 108 points and just two clear of second-placed Rochdale, who would resort to gaining promotion through the play-offs following a dramatic final-day clash for the ages between the two sides.

With the league title on the line for the victors, the encounter played out on a knife-edge at the Crown Oil Arena and 95 minutes of football were played before the deadline was broken when Emmanuel Dierseruvwe appeared to have won the contest for the hosts when he struck past York's Harrison Male.

The Ministermen only needed a point from proceedings, though, and capped off one of English football's most pulsating final-day showdowns after Josh Stones buried an all-important equaliser in the last kick of the game to shatter Rochdale hearts and take the fifth-tier title back to Yorkshire instead.

However, a major flashpoint emerged prior to Stones' leveller in the wake of Dieseruvwe's opening strike, which led Rochdale supporters to believe that they had won the affair in the very closing stages.

Dale fans promptly stormed the pitch in celebration, and in all the commotion, one of York's promotion heroes in Hiram Boateng appeared to have been pushed to the ground before retaliating in a manner that now leaves the midfielder shrouded in legal trouble.

Widely-shared social media footage at the time showed Boateng on the floor in the wake of Rochdale's goal, with the 30-year-old having seemingly been pushed over and subsequently goaded by celebrating supporters - and pinned down on the floor, too, it has been claimed.

The scenes were unsavory to say the least, as Rochdale fans invaded the pitch to taunt and antagonise York players despite the game still having numerous minutes of additional time to be played out.

As stewards acted to break up the fracas, Boateng responded by punching a home fan, who promptly fell to the floor himself.

It was quickly disclosed afterwards that the FA would be investigating the matter, and proceedings have now been taken up a notch.

That's because a fresh report published by The Sun on Monday evening has revealed that Boateng, who has made just four appearances for Scott Lindsey's side in League Two so far this season, could face jail after being charged with a criminal offence.

The investigation has been taken to court, where Boateng has been charged with using threatening, abusive or insulting behavior with intent to cause fear of or provoke violence.

It's said that the Crystal Palace academy product's case was heard with no pleas on Monday morning at Manchester magistrates' court, with the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) confirming the charges brought against the player in question.

A Home Office study has revealed which fanbases have seen the most arrests in English football, with those of some EFL clubs ranking high

Whether Boateng will actually spend time behind bars remains to be seen, of course, but the legal battle remains at large and it's caused quite the reaction from the many backers he has in his corner at York.

The former Exeter City and MK Dons star has retained the full backing of everybody at the LNER Community Stadium since the altercation, and club chairman Matt Uggla is among those to have spoken out in support of the popular midfielder.

Boateng, having joined York in the summer of 2025 following his departure from League One outfit Mansfield Town, played a leading role in the Ministermen's successful title charge during his debut campaign and has barely kicked a ball in anger this time around, with injuries limiting the well-travelled midfielder to just two fourth-tier starts.

Ironically, however, York faced Rochdale for the first time since the promotion-defining battle back in April, and with the fixture having been carried out in Greater Manchester, Lindsey's side would come out on top when Ollie Pearce scored the only goal of the game after 56 minutes, and Boateng himself was in the starting lineup.

Now, with the investigation against Boateng beginning to intensify following fresh developments, Uggla has responded to show his support and dismay at the charges being brought against the City starlet.

Speaking via his X account yesterday evening, Uggla wrote: "A fan runs onto the pitch to deliberately antagonise a player, yet it's Hiram who ends up facing a criminal charge.

"Where's the accountability for the person who invaded the pitch and provoked the situation? Absolutely ridiculous.

Uggla, of course, is far from the only figurehead to reserve strong backing for Boateng, who many believe was firmly within his right to retaliate after Rochdale supporters had committed a criminal offense in the first place by invading the field of play to antagonise opposition players.

Echoing the school of thought of many, this one fan called for the case to simply be thrown out of court in argument of injustice towards Boateng.

Another referred to the situation as "scandalous", citing the inarguable fact that one person had the right to be on the pitch and the other simply did not.

Indeed, the case has prompted cries for an enhanced systemic approach towards player safety and welfare in which greater protection and prevention from such events is provided, with several fans asking why the Dale supporter has not been identified and publicised for their own offences.

An Oldham Athletic supporter, meanwhile, has called for the fan to feel the same legal repercussions in an impassioned rant.

Whether or not Boateng was right for hitting out a fan has been hotly-debated online - and will be in the courts, of course - but this punter feels as though the midfield man did nothing wrong in the first place and the pitch-invader received just what they deserved in an act of "self defence" from York's promotion-winner.

However, not everybody has spoken in defence and support of Boateng.

It's clearly the general consensus, though others have argued that Boateng did not need to retailiate in such a fashion.

What do you make of the case? Was Hiram Boateng in the right here and should the York City midfielder's actions go unpunished, or does he deserve the legal charges? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

Rather interestingly, one York fan hopped over the other side of the fence and, in a claim that has not gone down too well among the City faithful, explained how Boateng's punch was unnecessary in spite of the wrongs of the aggravating supporter.

Whereas some Rochdale fans have slammed the behaviour of one of their own, others have taken a less-sympathetic stance towards Boateng and believe that his actions - regardless of whether the supporter was right to be on the pitch or not - cannot be allowed to go unpunished.

It's a controversial old case, and the direction of its travel will only be determined in due course.

For now, at least, all York supporters and power-brokers alike will intend on doing is continuing to defend the well-liked midfielder against the charges, which the overwhelming majority believe to be unjustified in light of what led to his actions.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.
